config.text: Top-down product mockup photograph of one single tall narrow vertical menu card, very elongated proportion of 10 by 21 centimetres, lying flat and centred on a pale warm grey linen tablecloth, soft even daylight, the whole card visible with margin around it. The card is thick uncoated deep burgundy cotton paper, colour sang-de-boeuf #560002. The only printing on the card is hot-foil stamping in two flat layers. Layer one, underneath: a fish, stamped in flat opaque matte white foil. Layer two, on top: a lamb, stamped in flat bright silver metallic foil, printed over the white fish and fully opaque where the two overlap, so the silver hides the white there. Each foil is one perfectly uniform solid area with crisp clean edges and a very slight debossed relief pressed into the paper. The drawing is made of bold, simple, flat shapes with thick strokes and a few large internal cut-outs, like a hand-carved linocut reduced to its essentials, readable from across a table. Plenty of empty burgundy paper around the figures. The card surface carries no lettering at all. Composition: like a two-colour overprint poster, the white fish stands vertically, head up, filling the central two thirds of the card; the silver lamb, in side profile at a similar large scale, is placed over it with a clear offset to the right and slightly lower, so roughly half of each animal overlaps the other and both remain fully readable.
